Continuity Drives Genesis Magma Racing’s 2027 Plans

Genesis Magma Racing has announced that it will keep the same six drivers who competed in its debut 2026 season for the 2027 FIA World Endurance Championship (WEC). The decision, confirmed on the team’s official media page, underscores a strategic focus on stability as the program moves into its second year of development for the GMR‑001 Hypercar.

Why the Same Drivers?

Team Principal Cyril Abiteboul explained that continuity is essential at this stage of the program. “Our drivers have built valuable knowledge of the GMR‑001 Hypercar and strong working relationships with our technical team. They have also developed a positive dynamic and genuinely enjoy working together. Retaining the same line‑up allows us to carry this experience and team spirit into 2027, continue developing the car efficiently and take further steps towards scoring points with both cars at every race,” he said.

Sporting Director Gabriele Tarquini added, “Our drivers understand the car, our working methods and what we need to improve. They work very well together and have built a strong relationship with the entire team, so we are very pleased to continue with this group next season.”

2026 Achievements That Shape 2027

Genesis Magma Racing’s first season delivered several notable results that will serve as a foundation for future progress:

  • Immediate competitiveness at the season opener in Imola.
  • First championship points earned by the #17 GMR‑001 Hypercar at the 6 Hours of Spa‑Francorchamps (only the second race).
  • Best overall finish to date: seventh place at Lone Star Le Mans.
  • Successful debut at Le Mans 24 Hours, meeting a key objective.
  • Top‑five performance for the #19 car at the 6 Hours of Fuji.
  • First pole position in the series, secured by Mathys Jaubert at the 6 Hours of Barcelona, just seven races into the debut campaign.

These milestones, combined with the drivers’ contributions to car development, give the team confidence that the current driver group can push for regular point‑scoring finishes in 2027.

Practical Implications for Fans and the Industry

  • Development speed: Retaining drivers who already understand the car’s nuances should accelerate aerodynamic and mechanical refinements, potentially narrowing the gap to leading manufacturers.
  • Team cohesion: The existing driver lineup has demonstrated strong chemistry, which can translate into consistent race strategy execution and reduced communication overhead.
  • Target setting: Genesis aims to score points with both cars at every race in 2027, a clear quantitative goal that fans can track throughout the season.

What Remains Unknown?

While the total number of drivers is confirmed, Genesis has not yet disclosed the exact driver assignments to its two cars for the 2027 season. Those details are expected to be announced ahead of the first race of the year. Until then, speculation will focus on how the team balances its experienced drivers across the #17 and #19 entries.

How Readers Can Verify

All official statements and the full announcement are available on Hyundai’s motorsport media page: [https://motorsport.hyundai.com/media-center/news/2026/wec/genesis-magma-racing-confirms-drivers-for-2027-fia-wec-season](https://motorsport.hyundai.com/media-center/news/2026/wec/genesis-magma-racing-confirms-drivers-for-2027-fia-wec-season). The source includes direct quotes from Abiteboul and Tarquini and outlines the team’s 2026 results.

Key Takeaways

  • Genesis Magma Racing will field the same six drivers in 2027.
  • The decision is rooted in the team’s desire to maintain momentum and deepen car development.
  • 2026’s results provide a solid baseline for aiming at regular point finishes.
  • Exact driver line‑ups for each car will be revealed closer to the season start.
  • Fans can follow the official link for any future driver announcements and race coverage.
